summary: The rate receipt answered the frequency question and let me retire two limitations that the evidence had settled. Twenty mixed-timer trials all showed a competing leader elected before the cut-off leader's confirmations stopped — competing leaders at 12ms to 41ms, with five to fourteen confirmations following each — and the two uniform controls showed neither a competing leader nor a confirmation after one, so the consequence is the ordinary outcome of that configuration rather than an unlucky phase. I appended that interpretation, marked the frequency question explained, and revised both standing accounts so they no longer carry a "single witness, frequency unknown" caveat: the child question now states the overlap as measured under per-node timers and separated under uniform ones, and the parent VerifyLeader account, with that receipt joined to its own mechanism receipt, states the consequence as quantified while keeping its scope explicit — the cluster must contain a nonvoter and its nodes must not share timers, and what the runs establish is an unsound basis for a consistent read rather than a delivered stale value. In the same update I pushed the consequence one step further and submitted it: the extended harness now has the first competing leader to appear commit an entry through the exported API and, on every confirmation, compares that leader's commit index with the cut-off leader's applied index. Native feedback from the local dry run, explicitly not retained evidence: all twelve mixed trials produced confirmations while the competing leader's commit index was already above the cut-off leader's applied index (commit 7 against applied 5, first such moment at 17-46ms), while both controls never elected a competing leader at all. If that reproduces in the retained run, it is the direct form of the stale-read precondition — a successful confirmation held at a moment when the cluster's committed state had already moved past what the confirming leader had applied.
